title: The Savoy Bearcats, Willie Lynch and Fess Williams
summary: Discussion of who played the Savoy then: the Savoy Bearcats with drummer Willie Lynch, and a clarinetist who was a great technician.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Was Don Kirkpatrick on piano?
Yeah. That's right.
It wasn't Elmer James on bass.
No, I think this was before Elmer's time.
It was before Elmer's time.
No, it wasn't Elmer. The name was Leon something.
Leon something.
Yeah, because we used to hang out together.
Now, did they have the two bands?
Yeah, there was the what'chacallit band there...
Not Fess. Savoy Bearcats?

Yeah, the Bearcats were there. I'm sure it was the Bearcats. Yeah, I think it was the Bearcats. Because I remember when Fess played there, there was a big opening for him, you know. I think Fess was away at that time.
Yeah, he was in Chicago.
Yeah, I think so.
Holmes (10/9) - 47
He was opening the Regal.
That's right. And then when he come back, they had a big opening for Fess. Yeah, the Bearcats was there. That's the band that Willie Lynch was in. He was the drummer in the Bearcats. That's right.
Yeah. And Billy Butler was in that band.
Yeah. Jay-Joe... That's right, Jay-Joe(?), clarinet player. Yeah, that's right. They were there. The Charleston Bearcats.
Not Charleston... The Savoy Bearcats.
The Savoy Bearcats.
Yeah, Willie Lynch formed that band.
Yeah.
It was a collective band, actually. They all had a part in it.
Well, see, when Willie left that band, then he got a band of his own. That was the beginning of the...
Yeah, Carmelo Jay-Joe(?).
Something like that, yeah.
I think he played with the reed upside-down.
I don't know. I know the ligature used to be upside-down, what holds the reed in there. Maybe some people thought the reed was. I don't know.
Ah, so maybe it wasn't.
Holmes (10/9) - 48
I don't know. I didn't look at them that close.
But he was quite a technician.
